page: Google Cloud Platform z4m-highmem-192-metal is a bare-metal storage-optimized server built on the x86_64 architecture. The server provides 192 dedicated virtual CPUs with no hypervisor layer, accompanied by 1536 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 8 GB of RAM per core. For local high-speed persistence, the instance is equipped with 180,389 GB of integrated NVMe solid-state storage across local SSD arrays.

Because the platform operates on bare metal without virtualization overhead, it delivers direct access to physical compute, memory, and NVMe controllers. It does not integrate dedicated GPU accelerators, making it unsuitable for GPU-reliant tasks. The massive NVMe capacity and memory density position it in a high-tier expenditure profile, where cost efficiency is realized through consolidating extreme I/O and large-scale data storage operations onto a single bare-metal node rather than managing multiple distributed nodes.

Google Cloud Platform z4m-highmem-192-metal is designed for enterprise storage and database workloads requiring vast local storage footprints and expansive system memory. Typical deployments include massive distributed databases, large-scale in-memory and hybrid data stores, high-throughput analytics pipelines, and heavy ETL systems processing terabytes of data directly on local NVMe arrays.
description: Google Cloud Platform z4m-highmem-192-metal is a bare-metal, storage-optimized instance running on the x86_64 processor architecture. Built for high-capacity local data throughput and intensive memory operations, the server delivers 192 dedicated vCPUs and 1536 GB of RAM, offering a high 8 GB of memory per core. The configuration includes an extensive local NVMe SSD storage array totaling 180,389 GB across 12 local SSDs, eliminating hypervisor overhead for direct hardware access. It operates without dedicated GPU acceleration and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. While carrying a substantial enterprise-grade operating cost, it achieves efficiency by allowing massive data consolidation and extreme I/O execution on a unified bare-metal footprint. This instance is specifically suited for high-scale storage and database applications, enterprise transactional databases, distributed storage nodes, memory-heavy data warehousing, and comprehensive ETL workloads processing large datasets locally.
